Details
This guidance provides information and outlines the core engineering and mathematics knowledge required for restricted, management level Certificates of Competency (STCW III/2 and III/3). The MCA General Engineering Science examinations are currently delegated to the International Association of Maritime Institutions (IAMI).
This is guidance to all Owners, Masters, Officers, Ratings and those concerned with maritime training. This guidance should be read with with MSN 1857 - Amendment 1 , MSN 1904 and replaces the syllabus published on UK seafarer careers: Training provision, information and examination syllabuses .

excerpts:
plot from multiple correspondence analysis (MCA)
Make the MCA (using a wrapper function around FactoMineR:MCA ) :
[](#cb3-1) library (ggfacto) [](#cb3-2) [](#cb3-3) data (tea,  package = "FactoMineR" ) [](#cb3-4) res.mca  <- MCA2 (tea,  active_vars = 1 : 18 )
Make the plot (as a ggplot2 object) and add a supplementary variable ( "SPC" ) :
[](#cb4-1) graph_mca  <- ggmca (res.mca, tea,  sup_vars = "SPC" ,  profiles = TRUE ,  text_repel = TRUE )
Use text_repel = TRUE to avoid overlapping of text, and obtain a more readable image (be careful that, if the plot is overloaded, labels can be far away from their original location).
Use profiles = TRUE to draw the graph of individuals : one point is added for each profile of answers.
Turn the plot interactive :
[](#cb5-1) ggi (graph_mca)
See
It may takes time to print, but really helps to interpret the MCA in close proximity with the underlying data.
